notes: Binary: scratchpad/langs/repocortex (version 'dev'). Each language was indexed in its own directory under scratchpad/langs/work/G2/idx/<language>; raw query output is in work/G2/out/<language>.{files,syms}.json.

Scoring unit: one definition site. For languages with multi-clause functions (Elixir, Erlang, Faust, redefinitions in Common Lisp) each clause head / definition form is one site, so several rows with the same name on different lines are each 'correct', not duplicates. Distinct-name figures are given where this matters (Elixir 39/52 names; Erlang 114 rows = 51 names).

'correct' can exceed (expected - missed) where the tool extracted real nested/local definitions that the convention did not require (D: 4 nested functions; Faust: 7 `with`-local definitions). Recall always uses expected definitions only.

wrong_kind counts labels that put a definition in a different category of the language (macro or method labelled 'function', record labelled 'function'). The tool's documented vocabulary merges (struct/enum/typedef -> 'class', module/namespace -> 'package') were NOT counted as wrong_kind but are mentioned per language.

parse_status 'partial' never came with an error message: parse_error was NULL for all 13 partial files (cue 4, devicetree 5, faust 2, crystal 1, d 1). 'ok' is not a guarantee either: crystal handler.cr and elixir float.ex are 'ok' yet lose definitions that are found when the surrounding code is removed.

Language detection findings: Erlang escript with extension .es is indexed as javascript (0 symbols); Faust .lib files are skipped with 'no grammar for this file type'; Common Lisp .l and .cl were detected correctly.
Synthetic probe files (not scored) were used only to confirm patterns seen in real files; they live in work/G2/probe/.
Nothing crashed or hung. Every index run finished in under 0.4 s wall time (reported Duration 29-194 ms).
All 12 languages could be tested. Device Tree has no Linguist sample folder, so its files come from the dtc test suite only.
